timestamp_derivation: After the whole authorized cleanup was implemented across Hotel Admin, edged, scd and the guest portal, and the full Go and UI suites plus the production build were run locally; before the author timestamp of the commit that introduces this receipt. Per T0091, in the order T0108 requires.

setup_activation_hung_and_the_cause_was_.symptom: Setup / Activation showed 'License active - finishing up...' indefinitely on PRE-LIVE.
setup_activation_hung_and_the_cause_was_.what_the_appliance_reported: enrolled=true, assignment assigned and adopted, api_mtls.mtls_ready=true, licence Active, activation_status='activated' -- and nats_mtls.connected=false.
setup_activation_hung_and_the_cause_was_.cause: The page required licOk && mtls && nats to reach the final stage. This appliance serves Central for LICENSING ONLY (T0071): the NATS transport is deliberately not opened. iam_v2.site_cloud_mode reads LICENSING_ONLY and Central's 4223 listener is not established, so the completion condition was unreachable by design. The appliance was correct; the page was wrong.
setup_activation_hung_and_the_cause_was_.fix: Completion follows the rule scd already used for activation_status -- enrolled + licensed + API mTLS, no NATS term. The defect existed twice, in currentStage() and in the complete flag. The real-time channel is no longer painted as a red 'Disconnected' fault; it reads 'Not used at this site' with the reason.
setup_activation_hung_and_the_cause_was_.not_masked: No loading state was hidden and no timeout added. The condition itself was wrong.

license_activation_and_cloud_duplication.before: Three screens answered one question. License, Setup/Activation and Cloud connection each showed appliance identity; two showed licence state; three showed mTLS or NATS.
license_activation_and_cloud_duplication.after: Cloud connection is retired as a page and redirects. Under the licensing-only model the link to Central exists to register the appliance, issue its certificate, carry the licence and enforce it -- so everything the page showed is licence state, certificate health or identity, and it is now a 'Connection to Central' card on License. Activation moved from Networking to System, beside License: first-time enrollment and ongoing licence administration are the same job at two points in its life.
license_activation_and_cloud_duplication.tls_kept_separate: The Hotel Admin TLS certificate page stays where it was and is untouched. It secures the local HTTPS an operator reaches this admin over, which has nothing to do with whether Central is reachable -- exactly the distinction the mission asked to preserve.
license_activation_and_cloud_duplication.nothing_removed_from_the_runtime: No Cloud, NATS or mTLS behaviour was changed. This is operator surface only.

the_contrast_defect_was_one_mapping.what: globals.css defines --muted as a quiet SURFACE and --muted-foreground as a quiet LABEL, with a comment saying they exist to be styled independently. Tailwind resolves text-muted to muted.DEFAULT, which was the SURFACE.
the_contrast_defect_was_one_mapping.consequence: 517 secondary labels across the admin rendered at 1.12:1 on a white card and 1.08:1 in dark. That is not low contrast; 1:1 is invisible. It is the grey text on every System screen.
the_contrast_defect_was_one_mapping.after: 5.28:1 light and 6.37:1 dark, both clearing WCAG AA. The three places that wanted the quiet panel now say muted-surface.
the_contrast_defect_was_one_mapping.pinned: A test resolves the Tailwind config, fails if DEFAULT is pointed back at the surface, computes both ratios, and asserts the OLD value would have failed -- so it cannot pass for an unrelated reason.

checkout_grace_history.after: One line per version -- version, terms summary, date, actor -- opening on demand for the full pinned terms, older versions behind a control, the in-force version marked.
checkout_grace_history.what_was_deliberately_not_done: No archive, hide or delete control. This is the append-only publication ledger: the provenance of what every departing guest was promised and the record a rollback is judged against. Hiding a row would make the version sequence lie by omission. The clutter was in the rendering, so that is where it was fixed.

config_history.after: A needs-attention filter (awaiting confirmation, rolled back, failed) and a fold for older entries, over the existing compact row-and-detail model.
config_history.no_deletion: A revision is what rollback rolls back TO and what the current configuration's provenance points at. Removing one does not tidy the list, it makes the remaining history misleading.

backups_became_a_feature.what_was_wrong: The screen listed public.backup_records, which nothing has ever written a row to on this appliance -- so it read 'No backups yet' forever, while the appliance retained 444 MB of deploy and rollback artefacts and ran a daily retention sweep that already knew its disk pressure, protected paths, pinned items and reclaimed space. All of it was real and none of it was reachable from Hotel Admin.
backups_became_a_feature.and_the_gap_underneath: There were no database backups at all. keep_db=7 was a retention policy for a category nothing produced.
backups_became_a_feature.now: Health from the sweep's own status document and the systemd timer; the retention policy as it is actually applied, including what is protected and never deleted; the artefact inventory with kind, size and age; a manual database backup under password step-up; download of any artefact; and verification.
backups_became_a_feature.no_live_restore: Deliberate. A live restore replaces running guest and configuration data and cannot be undone by clicking again. VERIFY loads a dump into a throwaway database, counts its tables and drops it -- answering the question an operator actually has about a backup without betting the site on it. The restore path is described on the page instead of being a button beside a download link.
backups_became_a_feature.honest_failure: A dump is written to .partial and renamed only on success, and a dump under 1 KB is discarded rather than recorded -- gzip of nothing still exits 0.

what_the_live_appliance_found._note: Six defects, none of which a test could have produced, because every one of them is about the appliance's own privilege, ownership or timing rather than about logic.
what_the_live_appliance_found.1_directory: edged runs as the unprivileged service user and /opt/stayconnect/backups is root-owned, so it could not create its subdirectory. Provisioned; the error now names the path and the cause instead of sending an operator to check disk space.
what_the_live_appliance_found.2_docker_socket: There is no pg_dump on the host and PostgreSQL runs in a container, so a dump means reaching the Docker socket -- which edged cannot, correctly. Docker group membership is effectively root; granting it to the process serving the operator HTTP surface would hand root to anything that got a foothold there. The dump moved to scd, which already runs as root and is already this appliance's privileged helper for certificates, licensing and PMS administration. Authorisation stays in edged: RBAC, step-up and audit.
what_the_live_appliance_found.3_file_group: scd writes the dump as root; edged serves the download as the service user. Mode 0640 alone left the file root:root, so 'group readable' meant readable by nobody who needed it. The download answered 500 until the group became the service group.
what_the_live_appliance_found.4_scratch_database: The deferred DROP of the verification database ran after the response was written, on a request context that was already cancelled, so it was killed before it executed and PRE-LIVE was left carrying a verify_* database. The cleanup now has its own background context and deadline, and logs if it still fails.
what_the_live_appliance_found.5_the_deadline: A good 23 MB dump was reported as failing to load. The scd log said 'signal: killed': edged's shared scd client gives up after 15 seconds, which is right for every other privileged call and fatal for a verification that takes minutes. Both sides now carry deadlines that match the work, and neither rides on the caller's context -- a client that gives up cannot leave a half-written archive or a killed load behind.
what_the_live_appliance_found.6_the_message_that_hid_it: That failure was reported as 'the dump did not load: (1 row)'. tailLine returns the final non-empty line and psql keeps printing normal output after an error, so the detail described the tail of a successful-looking transcript and cost a round of looking in the wrong place. The first ERROR/FATAL line is the cause now, and the raw error is logged either way.

backups_became_a_feature.the_ledger_was_removed_rather_than_reshi: public.backup_records exists and the old screen listed it, but NEITHER service role can write to it -- svc_edged holds SELECT only and svc_scd holds nothing. That is why nothing has ever inserted a row and why the screen read 'No backups yet' on an appliance holding 444 MB of artefacts. Granting INSERT is a migration this mission does not authorise, so the card is gone: the artefacts ARE the history, and who took each one is in the audit log, written through the same path as every other privileged action. Adding a second permanently-empty viewer beside the one I was sent to fix would have been the same defect with a new heading.
backups_became_a_feature.proven_live: A real 23,619,911-byte dump taken through the operator API under step-up; verified as ok=true across 141 tables; downloaded in full and checked as a valid gzip; the scratch database dropped; and the live site untouched throughout -- stays went 1810 to 1813 from ordinary PMS traffic, never from anything performed here.

guest_portal_redesigned.to: The Product Owner's reference: full-bleed hotel photograph, one centred white card, branded header, Guest Login and Account Login tabs, room-number and voucher/personal-account flows, a language selector upper right and an information affordance lower right.
guest_portal_redesigned.two_groups_not_seven_tabs: With every method enabled the old row carried seven tabs, unreadable on the 360px phone almost every guest uses. The question a guest can answer is 'am I staying here, or do I have a code?', so methods are grouped behind two doors. This is PRESENTATION: every panel is the same form it always was, and a test asserts each one is still rendered.
guest_portal_redesigned.device_addresses: The information panel shows the device's own IP and MAC. Both come from the connection and the ARP table -- never a header -- and a test forges X-Forwarded-For and X-Real-IP to prove a guest cannot make the page display an address that is not theirs. A guest who cannot tell reception their MAC cannot be helped by reception.
guest_portal_redesigned.responsive: One design language across desktop, tablet and phone; on a phone the card becomes the page rather than becoming a second design.

branding_became_a_designer.what_was_wrong: A textarea containing raw JSON, with no schema, no validation, no history and no rollback -- and nothing read it. The captive portal never fetched branding at all, so whatever an operator typed changed nothing a guest saw. It was write-only configuration behind a syntax check.
branding_became_a_designer.now: A designer for hotel name, logo, background, colours, typography, corner radius, wording and terms, with a live preview, publish under step-up, versioned revisions and rollback. The portal fetches the published design through a new guest-safe endpoint, so branding finally has an effect.
branding_became_a_designer.versioning_without_a_migration: The revisions live inside the existing tenants.branding document -- published design, working draft and bounded history. The internal representation is an implementation detail and the operator never meets it; no schema change was needed.
branding_became_a_designer.rollback_does_not_rewind: Rolling back re-publishes an earlier design as a NEW revision. Deleting the newer one would leave a record implying it never existed, which is the same class of lie as deleting an audit row.
branding_became_a_designer.advanced_mode_refuses_rather_than_saniti: Custom CSS and HTML are accepted; script, inline event handlers, javascript: URLs, frames, objects, EXTRA FORMS, CSS expression(), behavior: and @import are refused, and the refusal explains why. This page collects room numbers, surnames and voucher codes -- silently stripping a tag would teach an operator their template worked. Twelve adversarial spellings are asserted, not one canonical <script>.
branding_became_a_designer.a_bypass_found_while_writing_those_tests: A protocol-relative logo_url of the form //host/logo.png passed the leading-slash 'appliance path' check and resolved to an external host over the page's own scheme. Refused now, with its own test.

tests: 311 UI tests and the full Go suite, including five new portal-structure tests, five branding-validation tests covering twelve injection spellings, and three setup-completion tests pinned to the exact shape PRE-LIVE returns.
no_migration: None. No schema change was needed or made anywhere in this delivery.

constraints_observed.no_architecture_change: The licensing-only model was read and described, never altered. No Cloud, NATS or mTLS runtime behaviour was removed -- only duplicated operator surface.
constraints_observed.no_destructive_restore: No live restore was performed or offered. Verification runs against a throwaway database.
constraints_observed.no_audit_deletion: No authoritative history was hidden, archived or deleted -- not the grace publication ledger, not network revisions, not branding revisions.
constraints_observed.no_pms_or_financial: No PMS configuration change, no PMS write, no financial traffic.
